newsitem.title: UK: Stg close to highs vs mark, awaiting rate rise.
newsitem.headline: Stg close to highs vs mark, awaiting rate rise.

text.p: Sterling consolidated just below six-year highs above 2.97 marks, awaiting a likely rise in UK interest rates to be announced on Thursday.

The market expected a rate rise of at least 25 basis points to result from the two-day Bank of England monetary policy committee meeting, starting today, with some forex traders even betting on a half-point rise.
Even though traders expect the pound to take a breather until a rate decision is announced on Thursday, many expect it to hit the psychological 3.00-mark level in the near-term.

"The market continues to have 3.00 marks in its sights and it looks increasingly likely that we will push through this level over a one-month horizon," said Michael Lewis, economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
Insufficient measures in last week's budget to rein in consumer spending boosted rate rise expectations and helped propel sterling even higher.

The pound spurted to a fresh-six year high of 2.9758 marks in late European trading on Tuesday. After an early drop below 2.97 marks, it recovered to 2.9735/45 marks by 0915 GMT, little changed from 2.9730/40 late on Tuesday.

Economists said a surprise jump in underlying inflation, to 2.7 percent in June from 2.5 percent the previous month, may have been the last straw for the BOE. The government has an underlying inflation target of close to 2.5 percent.
"Certainly, yesterday's poor June inflation figures appear to have tipped the balance in favour of a rise...," said Tim Fox, treasury economist at Standard Chartered.
Sterling was likely to suffer some profit-taking in the aftermath of a rate rise before resuming its rally, traders said.

A positive technical outlook adds further impetus to sterling's strength. Technical analysts said the pound had good support in the 2.9500 area and even a drop below was only likely to attract buyers again for the next leg of the upmove.
